teaser.text: Centene sells health coverage, mainly through government-funded programs. It takes a payment, arranges covered care through a network, and pays providers when members use that care.

stock.opening: Centene's weighted forecast reaches $75.51 by October 2029, a 10% total return including dividends. It hinges on Centene repairing underwriting and making the earnings recovery durable.
stock.closing: The full Centene memo also covers Centene's business, management, rivals and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could Centene's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The forecast places the price at $48.80 in October 2027, a 29% decline including dividends. It reaches $75.51 in October 2029. The bear case carries 30%, the base case 55%, and the bull case 15%.

The weighted price is $48.80 in October 2027 and $61.80 in October 2028. Those outcomes represent declines of 29% and 10% with dividends included. The October 2029 weighted price is $75.51, a 10% total return. Against today’s $68.63, the October 2029 range runs from $22.85 in the bear case to $155.57 in the bull case.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Centene, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: The base case starts from the $175,000M 2026 premium and service revenue midpoint and assumes moderate growth with margins recovering from 1.35% to 1.60%. That produces the table’s earnings path. The bear case uses slower revenue growth and margins of 0.6% to 0.8%, reflecting medical-cost pressure and weaker Marketplace risk. The bull case reaches margins of 1.7% to 2.2%, supported by better pricing, claims management and Medicare Advantage approaching break-even. The base is anchored by Q2 HBR improvement and the $4.80 floor, but excludes the roughly $0.50 per-share settlement benefit that management says will not recur in 2027.

The bull case would require Medicaid rates to exceed medical trend, profitable Ambetter retention and sustained HBR improvement. Earlier Medicare Advantage break-even and resumed buybacks would provide the strongest confirmation.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Centene really make?

paragraphs.text: Operating cash flow fell to $154 million in 2024 from $8,053 million in 2023. It recovered to $5,088 million in 2025, helped by better pharmacy-rebate timing and higher claims liabilities. After $767 million of capital spending, the arithmetic remainder was $4,321 million, but it was not freely distributable parent cash.

earnings.title: Centene earnings date and guidance
earnings.meta_description: Centene's next results are expected on October 27, 2026; guidance sets 2026 EPS floors and the release will test medical costs.
earnings.opening: Centene's next results are expected on October 27, 2026. Watch whether medical costs followed expectations and the expected fourth-quarter loss remains contained.
earnings.closing: The full Centene memo also answers how Centene makes money, who it competes with, how management operates and what risks it faces.

paragraphs.text: Management’s September 16 guidance sets a full-year GAAP diluted earnings-per-share floor of $3.11 and an adjusted floor of $4.80. Earnings per share divides profit among shareholders; “diluted” also allows for possible future shares, such as employee awards. GAAP follows standard accounting rules. Adjusted EPS removes selected costs, including restructuring and acquisition-related amortization, so it can help compare operations, but it is not a complete measure of repeatable profit.

The operating test is whether premiums leave enough after medical care and overhead. The health benefits ratio, or HBR, measures the share of premium revenue spent on members’ care. At a 91% HBR, an illustrative $100 of premium leaves $9 for administration, financing, taxes and profit. Adjusted SG&A measures administrative costs such as employees and systems, but its denominator differs from HBR’s, so the ratios cannot simply be subtracted.

Seasonality makes the full-year target harder to judge. For 2026, management expects the third quarter to finish slightly above breakeven and the fourth quarter to produce a loss because prescription-drug and individual-insurance results vary during the year. The recovery therefore depends on current premiums covering current medical costs through the expensive later quarters. That is the backdrop against which analysts revise their forecasts.

blocks.heading: What has Centene's revenue and profit done over the last eight quarters?

paragraphs.text: The first half also included $50 million of optimization costs and $18 million of severance. Management identified approximately $0.50 per share of quarterly earnings tied to 2025 settlements that it did not expect to recur in 2027. The eight-quarter pattern therefore matters more than the latest headline result. Investors need recurring current-year margins after settlements and seasonality disappear.

blocks.heading: What should Centene watchers look for on October 27, 2026?

paragraphs.text: The first dated checkpoint is the October 27, 2026 earnings release. Investors will want to know whether medical costs followed expectations, whether the expected Q4 loss remains contained and how much of the first-half strength survives without settlement benefits. The 2027 individual-market lineup will offer a second test: better pricing should restore margins, not purchase membership growth at weak prices.
